newsitem.title: USA: PanAmSat satellite used in India TV service.
newsitem.headline: PanAmSat satellite used in India TV service.

text.p: PanAmSat Corp said on Wednesday its PAS-4 Indian Ocean Regional satellite would serve as the transmission platform for STAR TV's direct-to-home television service in India.
STAR TV is a unit of News Corp.

The STAR TV service, called Sky, would use seven Ku-band transponders on the PAS-4 satellite, which can beam dozens of television channels to subscribers in India using rooftop dishes as small as 65 centimetres in diameter, it said.

"Given the strong market response to this satellite, PanAmSat looks forward to expanding its services in the Indian Ocean region with the upcoming launch of the PAS-7 satellite," Frederick Landman, PanAmSat's president and chief executive officer, said.
PanAmSat said it conducted extensive tests of PAS-4's ability to provide high-quality, reliable direct-to-home transmissions to India in all weather conditions.
PAS-4, launched in August 1995, is located at 68.5 degrees east longitude and contains 16 C-band and 24 Ku-band transponders, the company said.
The satellite was also the transmission platform for direct-to-home services in South Africa and the Middle East, PanAmSat said.
PanAmSat said it would expand its satellite services in the Indian Ocean region with the launch of the PAS-7 satellite, scheduled for early 1998.

The PAS-7 satellite would be located in the same orbital position as PAS-4 to facilitate television channel expansion both for C-band program distribution and Ku-band direct-to-home services, the company said.
